source: The three ways couples commonly split a shared month, as personal-finance guides and couples' money columns describe them: equal halves, in proportion to income, or one pool. Names and one-line descriptions only; no survey sits behind them and none is a rule.
confidenceNote: Each mode is a convention people choose, not a benchmark, and this file does not say which is fair. The sentences describe when people tend to pick each one; a couple's own arrangement replaces them.
note: Read by engines/partner.js. The mode ids match household.partner.splitMode (equal | proportional | pooled). D-099.

modes.label: Equal halves
modes.sentence: Each pays half of the shared month, whatever each earns.
modes.whenChosen: People choose it when the two incomes are close, or when keeping the split simple matters more than matching it to pay.

modes.label: In proportion to income
modes.sentence: Each pays the share of the shared month that matches their share of the household's income.
modes.whenChosen: People choose it when the incomes are far apart, so that the same month costs each of them a similar slice of their pay.

modes.label: One pool
modes.sentence: All income goes into one pool, all shared costs come out of it, and what is left is saved together.
modes.whenChosen: People choose it when they think of the money as one household's rather than two people's, and are happy for either to spend from the pool.
